title: Cast a concrete test cylinder: two layers in the mold, each rodded 25 times through its depth, then struck off flat
instruction: Make a test cylinder from this batch of concrete.
context: Concrete field-testing technicians (civil engineering technicians, O*NET 17-3022.00, often ACI-certified) cast test cylinders from the concrete delivered to a job; the cylinders are later broken in compression, and the concrete is accepted or rejected on their strength. ASTM C31/C31M fills a 4 x 8 in cylinder consolidated by rodding in two layers: the first about half the mold, rodded 25 times throughout its depth with a 0.375 in (10 mm) rod, the strokes spread uniformly over the cross-section, then the outside of the mold tapped 10 to 15 times; then the rest, rodded 25 times with each stroke reaching about 1 in into the first layer, tapped again, and the top struck off to an even, flat surface. A cylinder filled in one go, rodded too few times or in one spot, or whose top layer is not rodded into the one below keeps voids, breaks low, and can get good concrete rejected.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. The scene is a 1:2.5 bench model of the 4 x 8 in procedure. All objects are fixed except the scoop, the rod and the float. A black plastic cylinder mold, 4.1 cm across and 8.1 cm deep inside (4.7 cm across outside, 8.4 cm tall, 107 mL), empty, stands with its axis at x 31, y 5. A round steel sample pan, 13 cm across inside and 5.5 cm deep, stands with its axis at x 32, y -10.5; it holds 1,300 g of fresh gray concrete (2.20 g/mL as placed), 4.5 cm deep, its top 4.75 cm up. A steel scoop (50 g with a weighted handle) lies on a white scoop stand at x 21, y -16: its red round handle, 2.5 cm across and 7 cm long, runs along y with its center at y -16, 8 cm up, on a post 1.6 cm wide; a neck runs down from the handle's +y end to a round bowl 3.9 cm across outside (3.6 cm inside, 2.6 cm deep, 26.5 mL level, about 31 mL or 69 g heaped) whose center is at y -8.25, resting on a 3.5 cm square pad. A steel tamping rod 5 mm across with a rounded tip, 8.6 cm long below a black grip block 3 x 3 x 2.5 cm (60 g in all), hangs by its block in the slot of a wooden rod rack at x 20.5, y 15: the fork's two prongs are 9.8 cm up, its slot 1.2 cm wide and open toward the robot, its post behind; the rod's tip is 1.2 cm above the table, and a yellow tape band on the rod 8.1 cm above its tip reaches the mold's rim when the tip is on the mold's floor. A hand float (50 g) lies flat at x 32, y 22: an aluminum blade 10 x 4 cm and 4 mm thick, its long side along x, with a gray post 1.2 cm square and 2 cm tall and a black knob 3 x 3 x 2.5 cm on top.
scoring: Scored on the final state, which must hold 1 s, from the record of how the mold was filled and rodded. A layer is concrete added between rod strokes that is at least a quarter of the mold deep (2 cm); up to 5 mm added in all after the second layer is a top-up, which C31 allows (a small quantity before striking off). A stroke is the rod's tip pushed at least 3 mm into the concrete and drawn back out. The trial scores 0 unless all of these hold: exactly two layers and no more than 5 mm added in all after them; the first layer's top between 35% and 65% of the mold's depth (2.8 to 5.3 cm above its floor; C31: about half); at least 25 strokes made while the first layer was on top with the tip reaching within 8 mm of the mold's floor (throughout its depth); at least 25 strokes made while the second layer was on top with the tip reaching at least 9 mm below the first layer's top (C31's about 1 in is 1.0 cm at this scale; 1 mm for the rod's give); each layer's 25 strokes spread over the cross-section, at least 3 strokes in each of at least 4 of 5 zones (within 5 mm of the axis, and the four 90-degree sectors 9 mm or more off it, just under half the bore's radius; C31: distributed uniformly over the cross-section); and, after each layer's 25th stroke and before the next layer goes in, 10 to 15 taps on the outside of the mold below its rim (the hand's outer surface, from the gripper's own shape and pose, coming within 1.5 mm of the mold's wall below the rim, then drawing back at least 1 cm; C31 allows an open hand on a plastic mold). It also scores 0 while a tool point is within 4 cm of the scoop handle's center, the rod's grip block or the float's knob, or within 2.5 cm of any other part of those tools, or with a tool point or fingertip within 1 cm of a tool's outline (a tool still held), while a tool is still moving or off the table, or with the rod or the scoop left in the mold or the float lying on it. Then: 1.0 when the top is struck off, the float's edge drawn over at least 90% of the mouth after the last stroke and the last concrete added, with nothing standing more than 2 mm above the rim and the mold filled to within 2% of its volume, and both arms are back home and still (each tool point within 3 cm of where it started); 0.9 for the same with the arms not home; 0.25 when the layers and rodding are right but the top is heaped, sunk or not struck off. Filling the mold in one go, rodding a layer 24 times or less or all in one spot, stopping the first layer's strokes short of the floor, rodding the top layer without reaching into the first, or tapping a layer fewer than 10 or more than 15 times all score 0, whatever the top looks like. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.9 and 1.0. In a real trial, count the strokes per layer and where each goes in on a top-down video, count the taps per layer, check each stroke's depth on a side-on video (the top view cannot show it) against tape bands on the rod (one at the mold's depth, one at half its depth plus 1 cm), check the first layer against a mark at half height on the outside of the mold, and lay a straightedge across the rim (no gap or bump over 2 mm).
run_limit: 6,400 steps (5 minutes 20 seconds at 20 Hz): the scripted demo takes 164 s (3,274 steps: four scoops, 50 counted strokes, 24 taps and a strike-off), and a policy gets about twice that
reset_notes: Empty and wash the mold and the scoop; remix the batch and refill the pan to 1,300 g; hang the rod back in its rack and lay the float in its place, both clean. The concrete in the mold is consumed.
fidelity: A 1:2.5 bench model of the 4 x 8 in procedure; counts (25 strokes, 10 to 15 taps) are unscaled. Concrete is a scored bulk model, not particles: 2.20 g/mL as placed to 2.40 rodded, layers recorded between strokes; taps are counted but change nothing. It has no weight or collision, so tools pass through it. Real trials use a non-setting sand-clay stand-in, not cement. Concrete above the rim is drawn orange.
